title: BCI speech decoding speed and accuracy
bottleneck: Decoding attempted speech from neural activity could restore communication to locked-in patients, but current systems achieve tens of words per minute with significant errors, far below natural speech (~150 wpm). Vocabulary is limited, decoding latency is high, and performance varies across users and sessions. Real-time, open-vocabulary, conversational decoding is unsolved.
why_it_blocks: Communication is the most urgent BCI application; slow, error-prone decoding leaves patients still effectively silenced. Speed and accuracy gaps keep neural speech from replacing even basic assistive devices.
current_state: Research systems decode sentences from motor cortex at improving rates, with large-vocabulary demos emerging. Robust, real-time, conversational speech BCIs are still in clinical research. Error rates climb with vocabulary size, so open-ended conversation remains far harder than constrained phrase decoding.
